To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
manganese exposure induces a significant increase in TH mRNA in substantia nigral and ventral tegmentum neurons and that manganese exposure induces reactive astrocytosis only in striatum.
chronic exposure to manganese induces changes in the dopamine and GABA systems in the nigrostriat system of aged rats.
chronic manganese treatment in 18-month-old male rats induced tyrosine hydroxylation, decreased glutamate decarboxylation and induced reactive gliosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms of action of neuroactive compounds in brain.
the effects of manganese on the nigrostriato-pallidal GABAergic pathway and the dopamine system.
the study of neurotoxicity of metals and pesticides and their possible role as risk factors for Parkinson's disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of Mn on the nigrostriat system are not the same as those observed in younger animals.
manganese treatment in aged rats induces a selective increase in the number of dopamine cells in the substantia nigra.

Mn treatment of aged rats results in an increase in TH mRNA in the substantia nigra but not in striatal neurons, a decrease in GAD mRNA in the globus pallidum, a decrease in mitochondrial SDH activity and an induction of astrocytic gliosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Mn exposure at this age and dose causes a significant decrease in SDH activity, an induction of TH and a decrease of GAD mRNA levels.
manganese treatment in aged rats induces a selective damage of nigrostriatal dopaminergic system, but not of the mesolimbic dopaminergic system.
the nigro-striatal pathway seems to be more susceptible to manganese than other dopaminergic systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nigro-striatal system could be damaged by manganese exposure in aged animals.
